paragraphs.source_en: As we saw there are numerous attributes associated to the Round Head anthropomorphic figures such as masks, sticks, bracelets, head protuberances (or horns), half-moons, skirt-like objects (Fig. 5-18; 5-19). They are mainly associated with male figures, whereas females do not usually possess them. This is an important distinction suggesting that the attributes were not just decorative elements but they were objects with special functions expressing possibly a particular piece of information.

paragraphs.source_en: Only two of the main elements, the sticks and head protuberances, are represented everywhere in the area of the Round Heads. The fact that the stick is attributed almost exclusively to men and not to women is likely to exclude its function as a digging stick, which is the characteristic female item among hunter-gatherers (Lee 1979). Indeed, some of them are rather elaborated, such as short sticks rounded on the top. Since they are often found on figures presenting other attributes, these sticks are probably symbolic and not practical. Sticks used by the Masai elder men signify wisdom and peace and play a role in boys' initiation rituals. In numerous African societies the clubs are also a phallic symbol representing sexual maturity of initiated men (Goodman 1988).

units.source_en: Only two of the main elements, the sticks and head protuberances, are represented everywhere in the area of the Round Heads.

The fact that the stick is attributed almost exclusively to men and not to women is likely to exclude its function as a digging stick, which is the characteristic female item among hunter-gatherers (Lee 1979).
Indeed, some of them are rather elaborated, such as short sticks rounded on the top.
Since they are often found on figures presenting other attributes, these sticks are probably symbolic and not practical.
Sticks used by the Masai elder men signify wisdom and peace and play a role in boys' initiation rituals.
In numerous African societies the clubs are also a phallic symbol representing sexual maturity of initiated men (Goodman 1988).

paragraphs.source_en: Head protuberances in the paintings may represent feathers or horns attached on men's heads (Fig. 5-20). Their number varies from one up to six. Their form also differs, indicating perhaps different head attributes used for various occasions. This is true for example in case of the Great Gods whose shape of horns is unique for them and it is not represented on other figures. The current African religions are all concerned with fertility and growth, often represented by the symbol of horns (Mbiti 1969).
